title: Contributor curation and pruning checklist for tokens & components
creator: Ava Patel
description: Define a repeatable contribution and pruning workflow for the design system focused on tokens, buttons, tables, and charts. Deliverables: a contributor checklist, intake/RFC template for new components and tokens, a monthly pruning cadence, ownership matrix, and a small automated report (CI job) that highlights stale assets. Goal is to reduce UI drift, keep token surface minimal, and make deprecation decisions traceable.
acceptance_criteria: Published contributor checklist in Confluence with step-by-step gates (design review, engineering signoff, accessibility signoff, telemetry contract)
RFC intake template created and added to repo (docs/rfcs/design) with example filled for a synthetic chart update
Pruning cadence documented: criteria for 'stale' and 'deprecated' assets, 90/180 day retention windows, and a rollback/playbook for regressions
Ownership matrix published mapping components/tokens to primary/backup stewards
CI job (or scheduled script) that produces a weekly stale-assets report and links to candidate PRs for pruning

notes: Trade-offs discussed: strict pruning reduces surface area but risks breaking embedded apps. We prefer a phased deprecation with automatic warning banners in Console. The RFc template enforces a compatibility cost estimate and a roll-forward test plan.
